description: A battalion executive officer must approve the container assignments and loading controls for four categories of routine supplies moving by rail to a regional logistics hub.

shared_context.S1: Four empty containers are available for Friday's rail transfer: C-1, C-2, C-3, and C-4. All four have passed the routine pre-movement inspection and are accepted by the rail carrier.
shared_context.S2: The shipment contains battery modules, packaged lubricants, clinic coolers, and boxed repair parts.
shared_context.S3: The rail carrier accepts the completed load at the transfer yard at 1600 on Friday, and loading begins at 0800.
shared_context.S4: Maj. Alvarez approves the final container plan and directs any required handling controls.
shared_context.S5: The unit's normal Friday movement-control huddle reviews each shipment category, container assignment, and loading control before the manifest is signed.

PF1.text: The battery modules require a vented, grounded container and must be assigned to C-2; Capt. Morgan confirmed this in the supplier's packing certificate this morning, but the certificate has not yet been attached to the consolidated manifest.

PF2.text: The packaged lubricants must be kept in the liquid-segregation container C-3 and cannot be loaded with clinic or battery cargo; SFC Patel received the updated shop packaging sheet yesterday, but it has not been entered into the movement-control worksheet.

PF3.text: The clinic coolers require continuous refrigeration and must use C-1, with shore power connected and verified by 0700 Friday; Lt. Brooks received the clinic shipping instruction from the medical warehouse this morning, but it is still being checked against the clinic's dispatch list.

PF4.text: The boxed repair parts must use C-4 because their combined pallet weight is exactly 1,800 kilograms, and the pallets must be axle-balanced during loading; WO1 Grant confirmed the scale reading at the yard this afternoon, but the amended weight note is not yet on the signed movement packet.

acceptance_conditions: Battery modules must be assigned to C-2.
Packaged lubricants must be assigned to C-3.
Clinic coolers must be assigned to C-1.
Boxed repair parts must be assigned to C-4.
Clinic shore power must be verified by 0700 Friday.
A battery grounding inspection commitment must be recorded.
A liquid-segregation commitment must be recorded.
A continuous-refrigeration commitment must be recorded.
An axle-balanced loading commitment must be recorded.
The battery packing requirement must be cited in the justification.

content_checks.C6: any('grounded' in c['detail'] or 'grounding' in c['detail'] for c in commitments)
content_checks.C7: any('liquid-segregation' in c['detail'] for c in commitments)
content_checks.C8: any('continuous refrigeration' in c['detail'] for c in commitments)
content_checks.C9: any('axle-balanced' in c['detail'] or 'axle-balance' in c['detail'] for c in commitments)

decisive_facts.why: The supplier certificate changes the battery assignment to C-2 and adds the required grounded-container control.
The packaging sheet changes the lubricant assignment to C-3 and requires a liquid-segregation control.
The medical shipping instruction changes the clinic cooler assignment to refrigerated C-1, fixes shore-power verification at 0700 Friday, and requires continuous refrigeration.
The exact 1,800-kilogram weight changes the repair-parts assignment to C-4 and requires axle-balanced loading.
